rows.councilName: National Dental Commission (formerly Dental Council of India)
rows.text: In India, dentists register with their State Dental Council; the National Dental Commission's Ethics and Dental Registration Board keeps the national register (formerly the Dental Council of India; its site is still dciindia.gov.in).
rows.stepsLine: Dentists in India register with their State Dental Council.

rows.text: In India, doctors register with their State Medical Council; the National Medical Commission's Ethics and Medical Registration Board keeps the National Medical Register.
rows.stepsLine: Doctors in India register with their State Medical Council.

rows.text: In India, vets are entered on their State Veterinary Register where the state has a council; the Veterinary Council of India keeps the Indian Veterinary Practitioners Register.
rows.stepsLine: Vets in India apply to be entered on their State Veterinary Register.

rows.text: Nurses in India register with their State Nursing Council. The Indian Nursing Council sets nursing education standards and recognises qualifications: 8th Floor, NBCC Center, Plot No. 2, Community Center, Okhla Phase-I, New Delhi 110020; phone +91-11-66616800; email nodalofficer.inc@gov.in — https://indiannursingcouncil.org
rows.stepsLine: Nurses in India register with their State Nursing Council, not with the Indian Nursing Council.

rows.text: State Pharmacy Councils register pharmacists in India (Pharmacy Act, section 32(2)). The Pharmacy Council of India, the statutory body under the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (Pharmacy Act 1948), is the national regulator — https://pci.gov.in (this new site may not open from outside India).
rows.stepsLine: Pharmacists in India register with their State Pharmacy Council, not with the Pharmacy Council of India.

rows.text: Office for doctors in Malaysia: Malaysian Medical Council — https://www.mmc.gov.my. Its home page has a search for registered medical practitioners but does not state its own role, so whether it is the registering body is not confirmed yet.
Office for nurses in Tanzania: Tanzania Nursing and Midwifery Council — https://www.tnmc.go.tz. Its home page gives only its name, so whether it is the registering body is not confirmed yet.

rows.councilName: National Council of State Boards of Nursing
rows.text: For nurses in the United States: the National Council of State Boards of Nursing's official page, checked 2026-11-03, is the place to read this. It says nursing is regulated together with its member boards; the board of your own state is the one to ask.
For doctors in the United States: the Federation of State Medical Boards' own page could not be read on 2026-11-03; this is still being looked for.
For nurses in Iran: the Iranian Nursing Organization's own page could not be read on 2026-11-03; this is still being looked for.

Vets in Australia register with the veterinary board of the state or territory where they will work. The Australasian Veterinary Boards Council is the council of those boards; it does not register vets itself — https://avbc.asn.au/about/avbc-member-registration-boards/
rows.stepsLine: Apply directly to the veterinary board of the state or territory where you will work; the Australasian Veterinary Boards Council lists them.

PNMC's own registration page sets out two ways: online through its portal, or on a paper form with a bank fee slip, two photos and attested copies of the CNIC, diplomas or degrees, Matric and domicile certificates.
PMDC's home page says registration is done through its online portal: https://portal.pmdc.pk
